title: Berlin's Most Beautiful U-Bahn Stations - Quick Summary
items: **Three of the best are within four minutes of Alexanderplatz.** Rotes Rathaus, Museumsinsel and Unter den Linden all sit on the U5 extension that opened on 4 December 2020, and the walking-tour route passes directly over two of them.

**Museumsinsel is the one to see first.** A deep blue barrel vault carrying **6,662 points of light**, 16 metres down, taken from Schinkel's 1816 stage set for The Magic Flute. It opened seven months late, on 9 July 2021, because the ground under the Spreekanal had to be frozen first.

**Klosterstraße hides tiles from the Ishtar Gate project.** The 1913 Grenander station one stop east of Alexanderplatz has stylised palms in glazed tile, made with the same brick technique as the gate in the Pergamon Museum, from leftovers. With the Pergamon closed until the 2030s for the gate itself, this is currently the closest you can get.

**The cathedral-like one is a real trip.** Heidelberger Platz on the U3 is 28 minutes from Alexanderplatz: a cross-groin vault on stone piers, opened 12 October 1913, because Wilmersdorf paid for stone instead of steel.

**The colourful 1980s stations are all on one U7 run.** Rohrdamm, Paulsternstraße, Zitadelle, Altstadt Spandau and Rathaus Spandau are 40 to 48 minutes out, all by Rainer G. Rümmler. Treat it as a Spandau old town day with a good ride attached.

**Buy the right ticket.** A single AB ticket is **€4.00** and covers 120 minutes in one direction with no return, so an out and back needs two. Once you head to more than one corner of the city, the **€11.20** 24-hour AB ticket is cheaper. Prices checked on 26 August 2026.
